identity.name: Sodium methyl p-hydroxybenzoate
synonyms: p-carboxylic acid methyl ester sodium salt

function.mechanism: Paraben-class preservative that suppresses microbial growth in foods; regulatory uses are antimicrobial and GMP-limited.

adi.basis: 2004 EFSA AFC group ADI 0-10 for methyl and ethyl parabens and their sodium salts (E214-219 context)

efsa.key_finding: EFSA set a group ADI for methyl/ethyl parabens and sodium salts; propyl paraben was excluded from the group ADI.

fda.notes: Title 21 directly lists methylparaben (methyl p-hydroxybenzoate) as GRAS under GMP with a current GMP maximum of 0.1% in food; a direct section heading for sodium methyl p-hydroxybenzoate was not identified in the fetched Title 21 text.

adi.basis: WHO JECFA methyl p-hydroxybenzoate entry reports group ADI 0-10 (sum of ethyl and methyl esters); FAO INS 219 sodium methyl p-hydroxybenzoate page shows no evaluations.

concerns.summary: Recent literature characterizes paraben estrogenic activity as weak but notes cumulative/repeated exposure as a risk-assessment concern.
Non-human studies reported reproductive/developmental effects after methylparaben exposure (e.g., zebrafish maternal exposure model).

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA 2004 retained a group ADI for methyl/ethyl parabens and sodium salts and did not identify a comparable concern for methyl/ethyl as for propyl paraben.
U.S. CFR places methylparaben in the GRAS direct-food-substance framework with GMP limits.

populations: High cumulative consumers of paraben-containing foods
Children (higher intake per kg body weight)
adi_exceedance.notes: A 2025 scoping review reported that cumulative exposure from multiple food sources could exceed ADI in some contexts.

risk_assessment.rationale: Regulatory frameworks and ADIs exist, but bounded ADI values, cumulative exposure concerns, and recent mechanistic/non-human toxicity signals support a moderate-caution profile rather than limited or high.
key_factors: EFSA group ADI 0-10 mg/kg bw/day for methyl/ethyl parabens and sodium salts
FDA methylparaben GRAS listing with GMP and 0.1% current GMP maximum
WHO JECFA group ADI 0-10 for methyl/ethyl esters; sodium INS 219 page with no separate evaluation
Recent PubMed evidence flags cumulative exposure and endocrine/reproductive concern signals
